On October 15, with the help of independent security researchers, we identified and resolved a vulnerability affecting a third-party integration on the ChangeNOW website.

ChangeNOW’s transaction infrastructure was not affected, and client funds were secure throughout.

We currently have no evidence that it was exploited. But we also can’t assume that the researchers who reported it were the only ones to find it. Because of that, we’re looking at the different scenarios and warning clients about the information that could potentially have been exposed. This may include email addresses and transaction details.

For now, the main thing clients should watch out for is phishing. Always verify the sender of unexpected messages, avoid suspicious links, and never share your passwords, private keys, or seed phrases. Our official support email is support@changenow.io.

We’re launching NOW AI, a security initiative focused on identifying vulnerabilities earlier, and strengthening protection across all ChangeNOW products.

Today's discovery has accelerated its launch. More details on NOW AI will be published soon on a dedicated page on the ChangeNOW website.

📄 Iran condemns Colombia’s move to open embassy in occupied al-Quds

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The Iranian Foreign Ministry has strongly condemned Colombia’s action to open an embassy in occupied al-Quds as contrary to the UN Charter and international law.

In a statement released on Thursday, the ministry strongly condemned the Colombian government’s action of opening an embassy in occupied al-Quds, considering it contrary to the Charter of the United Nations and the fundamental principles of international law.
​
The statement added that al-Quds is an inseparable part of Palestinian territory, and all states are obligated under international law to refrain from any action that amounts to recognition of the Israeli regime’s occupation.
​
It further noted, “Undoubtedly, the alignment of Colombia’s current governing authorities with an occupying and genocidal regime, and the legitimization of the occupation of Palestinian territory, stand in clear contradiction to the aspirations for independence and justice that have shaped a significant part of the history of the struggles of the people of Colombia and Latin America.”
​
“The Colombian governing authorities’ action in opening the country’s embassy in occupied al-Quds runs counter to Colombia’s international legal obligations concerning respect for the right of peoples to self-determination and amounts to endorsing occupation and violating the Palestinian people’s right to self-determination. The Colombian government must accept responsibility for the consequences of its immoral decision, which is contrary to international law,” the ministry added.
